docs.title: CALC-001 — Tritium Decay Constant
docs.text: CALC 001 — Tritium Decay Constant Calculation ID Source Quantity t {1/2} = 12.32\pm0.02\ {\rm y} Source: Equation \lambda = \frac{\ln2}{t {1/2}} Therefore: \lambda = 0.05626195\ {\rm y^{ 1}} Using a Julian year: 1\ {\rm y} = 365.25\times86400 = 31\,557\,600\ {\rm s} gives: t {1/2} = 388\,789\,632\ {\rm s} and: \lambda = 1.78283\times10^{ 9}\ {\rm s^{ 1}} Approximate propagated uncertainty: u(\lambda) \approx 2.89\times10^{ 12}\ {\rm s^{ 1}} Result

docs.title: CALC-002 — Hydrogen Hyperfine Wavelength
docs.text: CALC 002 — Hydrogen Hyperfine Wavelength Calculation ID Measured frequency: \nu = 1\,420\,405\,751.768\ {\rm Hz} Source: Using: \lambda = \frac{c}{\nu} with exact SI speed of light: c= 299\,792\,458\ {\rm m\,s^{ 1}} gives: \lambda = 0.21106114054\ {\rm m} or: \lambda = 21.106114054\ {\rm cm} This is the origin of the usual description: The measured frequency is more precise than the rounded phrase "21 cm."

docs.title: CALC-003 — D-T Fusion Q-Value
docs.text: CALC 003 — D T Fusion Q Value Calculation ID Reaction: {}^2H+{}^3H \rightarrow {}^4He+n Using atomic masses: m D = 2.01410177812\ {\rm u} m T = 3.0160492779\ {\rm u} m {^4He} = 4.00260325413\ {\rm u} and neutron mass: m n = 1.00866491595\ {\rm u} The atomic electrons balance between the initial D+T atoms and final neutral He atom. Mass difference: \Delta m = m D+m T m {^4He} m n \Delta m = 0.01888288594\ {\rm u} Using the CODATA 2022 atomic mass energy equivalent: 1\ {\rm u}\,c^2 = 931.49410372\ {\rm MeV} gives: Q = 17.5892969\ {\rm MeV} or conventionally: \boxed{ Q\approx17.6\ {\rm MeV} } The formal uncertainty from the listed mass uncertainties is only of order: 2.3\times10^{ 6}\ {\rm MeV} before considering source covariance and evaluation details.

docs.title: Hydrogen — People and Intellectual Lineage
docs.text: Hydrogen — People and Intellectual Lineage Purpose Hydrogen science did not arise from one discovery. MAT distinguishes: This prevents attribution from becoming a simple list of famous names. 1. Early Hydrogen Chemistry Robert Boyle Role: Contribution: Described production of the gas later recognized as hydrogen through reactions involving metals and acids in the seventeenth century. MAT does not assign Boyle sole discovery of hydrogen as an element. Henry Cavendish Role: Contribution: Systematically studied what he called inflammable air and established important physical and chemical characteristics of the gas. Common historical attribution gives Cavendish major credit for identifying hydrogen as a distinct substance. Antoine Lavoisier Role: Contribution: Placed hydrogen into the developing modern chemical framework and gave it the name derived from its relationship to water formation. 2. Hydrogen Spectroscopy Johann Jakob Balmer Role: Contribution: Identified the mathematical regularity of the visible atomic hydrogen spectral series now called the Balmer series. Relationship: Johannes Rydberg Role: Contribution: Generalized the mathematical description of atomic spectral series. Hydrogen became a central test system for the Rydberg relationship. Niels Bohr Role: Contribution: Used hydrogen as the central atomic example in the early quantized atomic model. The Bohr model is historically important and predicts major hydrogen energy level relationships. MAT classifies it as: rather than the final modern quantum description. 3. Modern Quantum Description The following contributors are primarily linked through the scientific principles used to describe hydrogen rather than through discovery of Hydrogen itself. Max Planck Relationship: Erwin Schrödinger Relationship: Hydrogen became one of the principal exactly solvable quantum systems of the Schrödinger framework. Max Born Relationship: Relevant to: Werner Heisenberg Relationship: Wolfgang Pauli Relationship: Paul Dirac Relationship: 4. Electromagnetism and Field Response Michael Faraday Relevant to: electromagnetic induction; field concepts; electrochemistry. James Clerk Maxwell Relevant to: Hydrogen spectroscopy, radiation and plasma behavior rely on electromagnetic theory. Hendrik Lorentz Relevant to: \mathbf F = q( \mathbf E+\mathbf v\times\mathbf B ) and charged hydrogen/plasma states. Pieter Zeeman Relationship: Johannes Stark Relationship: 5. Hydrogen Isotopes Harold C. Urey Role: Urey led the scientific search that established heavy hydrogen. He received the 1934 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for the discovery. George M. Murphy Role: Murphy worked with Urey on the spectroscopic identification of heavy hydrogen. Ferdinand G. Brickwedde Role: Brickwedde produced enriched liquid hydrogen fractions at the National Bureau of Standards that enabled the heavy isotope's spectral signature to become clearly measurable. Edward W. Washburn Role: Associated with subsequent electrolytic enrichment/separation work involving deuterium. 6. Tritium and Heavy Hydrogen Nuclear Physics Ernest Rutherford Role: Mark Oliphant Role: Paul Harteck Role: Rutherford, Oliphant and Harteck published major 1934 experiments on transmutation using heavy hydrogen. These experiments form part of the historical lineage of hydrogen isotope nuclear physics and tritium production. 7. Cryogenic Hydrogen James Dewar Role: Contribution: Successfully liquefied hydrogen in 1898 and subsequently produced solid hydrogen. This forms part of the intellectual lineage of: 8. Precision Hyperfine Measurement The following researchers are linked directly to the precision Hydrogen hyperfine measurement used by MAT: Relationship: Reported frequency: 1\,420\,405\,751.768\ {\rm Hz} 9. Modern H₂ Thermodynamics J. W. Leachman R. T. Jacobsen S. G. Penoncello E. W. Lemmon Role: Contribution: Reference equations of state for: These models are used in the MAT thermodynamic branch rather than treating all molecular hydrogen as one state.

docs.title: 0002 — Helium — He
docs.text: 0002 — Helium — He 0. Record Navigation MAT Reference Previous Primary Record Current Record 1. Elemental Identity Property Value Unit / Status : MAT ID MAT:0002 — Element Helium — Symbol He — Atomic number 2 dimensionless Proton count 2 proton Neutral electron count 2 electron Period 1 — Group 18 noble gas Block s — Ground electron configuration 1s² — Ground electronic level \(^{1}S 0\) — Standard atomic weight 4.002602(2) — Primary sources: 2. Closed Shell Ground State Neutral ground state helium has: 1s^2 with ground level: {}^1S 0 The two electrons occupy the 1s orbital with opposite spin projection in the ground state configuration. This produces a closed electronic shell. Helium is therefore chemically much less reactive under ordinary conditions than Hydrogen. docs.title: Helium — People and Intellectual Lineage
docs.text: Helium — People and Intellectual Lineage Pierre Janssen Role: Associated with observation of the solar spectral line that preceded terrestrial isolation of Helium. Norman Lockyer Role: Interpreted the solar spectral feature as evidence for a previously unknown element. Edward Frankland Role: Associated with the naming of Helium with Lockyer. William Ramsay Role: Linked to establishing Helium on Earth through gas released from mineral material. Per Teodor Cleve and Abraham Langlet Role: Part of the independent terrestrial Helium identification lineage. Heike Kamerlingh Onnes Role: In 1908 Onnes successfully produced liquid Helium, opening a major new low temperature regime. ([Nobel Prize][3]) Pyotr Kapitza Role: Kapitza's experiments established the extraordinary flow behavior of He II and identified it as a superfluid. ([Nobel Prize][4]) John F. Allen Role: A. D. Misener Role: Allen and Misener independently reported the unusual flow behavior of liquid Helium II in the same historical period as Kapitza. Lev Landau Role: Developed the theoretical description of quantum collective excitations in liquid Helium, including the phonon/roton framework. ([Nobel Prize][5]) David M. Lee Douglas D. Osheroff Robert C. Richardson Role: Their 1972 experiments established superfluid phases of ³He. They shared the 1996 Nobel Prize in Physics for that discovery. ([Nobel Prize][6]) Anthony J. Leggett Role: Linked to theoretical understanding of superfluid ³He and more general macroscopic quantum phenomena. Classification Rule Do not collapse these roles into: The lineage distinguishes: These are different contributions.

docs.title: Lithium — People and Intellectual Lineage
docs.text: Lithium — People and Intellectual Lineage Johan August Arfwedson Role: Contribution: Identified Lithium as a new alkali element while analysing petalite in 1817. Jöns Jacob Berzelius Role: Arfwedson worked in Berzelius's laboratory. William Thomas Brande Role: Produced a small quantity of Lithium metal electrolytically in 1821. Robert Bunsen Role: Augustus Matthiessen Role: Bunsen and Matthiessen obtained sufficient bulk Lithium by electrolysis of molten Lithium chloride in 1855. John Cockcroft Role: Ernest Walton Role: Their accelerated proton experiment on Lithium demonstrated artificial nuclear transmutation and produced alpha particles. Lithium Ion Battery Lineage M. Stanley Whittingham Role: Contribution: Developed an early rechargeable Lithium battery using a host structure capable of reversible Lithium insertion. John B. Goodenough Role: Contribution: Developed high voltage Lithium cobalt oxide cathode chemistry, greatly increasing useful cell voltage. Akira Yoshino Role: Contribution: Developed a practical rechargeable architecture using carbonaceous negative electrode materials rather than metallic Lithium. docs.text: Beryllium — People and Intellectual Lineage René Just Haüy Role: Haüy suspected that beryl and emerald contained an unknown constituent and encouraged chemical investigation. Louis Nicolas Vauquelin Role: In 1798 Vauquelin identified the new element in beryl/emerald material. He did not isolate pure metallic Beryllium. Friedrich Wöhler Role: Wöhler isolated metallic Beryllium in 1828 through reduction chemistry involving Beryllium chloride. Antoine Bussy Role: Bussy independently isolated metallic Beryllium in 1828. MAT therefore distinguishes: from: Neutron Discovery Lineage Walther Bothe Role: Herbert Becker Role: Bothe and Becker observed unusually penetrating radiation when Beryllium was bombarded with alpha particles. Irène Joliot Curie Role: Frédéric Joliot Curie Role: The Joliot Curies showed that Beryllium radiation could eject energetic protons from hydrogen containing material. James Chadwick Role: Chadwick demonstrated in 1932 that the penetrating radiation was consistent with a neutral massive particle: Relationship: Beryllium therefore has a direct place in the experimental lineage of neutron discovery. Additional Principle Lineage Beryllium science also draws on principles associated with: These people are linked to theories, measurement methods or scientific frameworks. They are not all direct Beryllium discoverers. docs.title: Boron — People and Intellectual Lineage
docs.text: Boron — People and Intellectual Lineage Louis Joseph Gay Lussac Role: In 1808 Gay Lussac and Thénard produced an impure elemental Boron preparation through reduction chemistry. Louis Jacques Thénard Role: Worked independently of Davy's London work in the 1808 Boron isolation period. Humphry Davy Role: Davy independently obtained Boron containing elemental material in 1808. The historical products were not today's standard of ultra high purity elemental Boron. Henri Moissan Role: Produced purer Boron later in the nineteenth century. Ezekiel Weintraub Role: Produced highly purified Boron using Boron halide/hydrogen processing. Borane and Multicentre Bonding Lineage William N. Lipscomb Role: Lipscomb and collaborators determined Borane structures and developed a deeper understanding of their unusual electron deficient bonding. His work showed that conventional two centre/two electron bonding alone could not adequately explain the Borane family. He received the 1976 Nobel Prize in Chemistry: MAT relationship: Kenneth Wade Role: Wade developed electron counting rules linking skeletal electron pair counts to families of polyhedral cluster structures. Canonical classes include: For a closo cluster with \(n\) vertices: N {\rm SEP}=n+1 skeletal electron pairs. The rules are structural predictors and organizing principles. They are not universal laws for every Boron containing structure. D. Michael P. Mingos Role: Extended and generalized cluster electron counting concepts across main group and transition metal cluster chemistry. Eluvathingal D. Jemmis Role: Developed the mno framework for condensed/macropolyhedral cluster systems. This extends the intellectual lineage from isolated polyhedra toward connected cluster architectures. High Pressure Boron Lineage Artem R. Oganov Role: Associated with the identification and structural interpretation of \(\gamma B {28}\). Jiuhua Chen Role: Associated with experimental characterization of \(\gamma B {28}\). Carlo Gatti Role: Contributed to analysis of the unusual bonding/charge transfer character in \(\gamma B {28}\). docs.title: CALC-001 — Triple-Alpha Net Q-Value
docs.text: CALC 001 — Triple Alpha Net Q Value Net reaction: \[ 3\,{}^4He \rightarrow {}^{12}C \] Using: \[ m({}^4He)=4.00260325413\ u \] and: \[ m({}^{12}C)=12\ u \] the mass difference is: \[ \Delta m = 3m({}^4He) m({}^{12}C) \] \[ = 0.00780976239\ u \] Using: \[ 1u\,c^2=931.49410372\ {\rm MeV} \] gives: \[ \boxed{ Q = 7.274748\ {\rm MeV} } \] The stellar reaction proceeds through intermediate nuclear states, especially transient 8Be and the resonant 12C Hoyle state. The net Q value must not be confused with the Hoyle state excitation energy.

docs.title: CALC-002 — Carbon-14 Beta Decay Q-Value
docs.text: CALC 002 — Carbon 14 Beta Decay Q Value Reaction: {}^{14}C \rightarrow {}^{14}N + e^ + \bar{\nu} e Using neutral atomic masses: m({}^{14}C) = 14.0032419884\ u m({}^{14}N) = 14.00307400443\ u gives: \Delta m = 0.00016798397\ u and: \boxed{ Q \beta \approx 0.1564761\ {\rm MeV} } or approximately: 156.476\ {\rm keV} This is the total beta decay energy available to the decay products. It is not the energy of every emitted electron. The beta particles occupy a continuous energy spectrum because energy and momentum are shared with the antineutrino and recoiling daughter.

docs.title: CALC-003 — Carbon-14 Decay Constant

Smithson Tennant Role: Tennant demonstrated that diamond and ordinary carbonaceous material produce the same Carbon dioxide product under combustion, strengthening the conclusion that diamond is Carbon. docs.text: Nitrogen — People and Intellectual Lineage Henry Cavendish Role: Produced Nitrogen rich residual gas through removal of reactive components from air. He did not establish it as a new element. Joseph Priestley Role: Also obtained gas depleted in oxygen and observed its inability to sustain ordinary combustion or animal respiration. Daniel Rutherford Role: In 1772 Rutherford described the residual gas and recognized it as a distinct component of air. MAT distinguishes: from: Source: Antoine Lavoisier Role: Associated with the historical name: reflecting the inability of Nitrogen rich air to sustain animal life. Jean Antoine Chaptal Role: Coined the name: Source: Industrial Nitrogen Fixation Fritz Haber Role: Established practical laboratory synthesis: N 2+3H 2 \rightleftharpoons 2NH 3 under elevated pressure and temperature. Nobel Prize in Chemistry: Source: Robert Le Rossignol Role: Worked with Haber on the laboratory apparatus used to demonstrate continuous ammonia synthesis. Carl Bosch Role: Converted Haber’s laboratory chemistry into industrial high pressure ammonia production. Nobel Prize in Chemistry: Source: Alwin Mittasch Role: Led extensive catalyst development work associated with industrial ammonia synthesis. Source: Gerhard Ertl Role: Used modern surface science methods to establish detailed mechanisms of catalytic reactions on solid surfaces, including key steps in ammonia synthesis on iron. docs.title: CALC-001 — Fluorine-18 Decay Energetics
docs.text: CALC 001 — Fluorine 18 Decay Energetics Parent: {}^{18}F Daughter: {}^{18}O Neutral atomic masses: M({}^{18}F)=18.00093733\ u M({}^{18}O)=17.99915961286\ u Atomic mass difference: Q {\rm EC} = [M({}^{18}F) M({}^{18}O)]c^2 \boxed{ Q {\rm EC} \approx1.65593\ {\rm MeV} } For positron emission: Q {\beta^+} = [M({}^{18}F) M({}^{18}O) 2m e]c^2 giving: \boxed{ Q {\beta^+} \approx0.63394\ {\rm MeV} } This corresponds to the approximate positron endpoint before nuclear recoil corrections. Decay branches: Important distinction: The positron subsequently annihilates with an electron, typically producing two approximately: 511\ {\rm keV} photons. The ¹⁸F decay branch used above is supported by radionuclide standardization work: roughly 96.86% β⁺ and 3.14% electron capture ; TUNL’s dedicated half life evaluation recommends 109.732 ± 0.011 min . ([ScienceDirect][2]) The F₂ counterexample also becomes stronger numerically: modern work gives \(D 0(F 2)\) around 154.92 ± 0.10 kJ/mol , reinforcing the original conclusion that Fluorine's extraordinary chemical reactivity does not originate from an exceptionally strong F–F bond. ([ACS Publications][3]) HF, by comparison, has \(r e=0.916808\) Å, \(\omega e=4138.32\ {\rm cm^{ 1}}\), and \(B e=20.9557\ {\rm cm^{ 1}}\) in the NIST diatomic compilation. ([NIST WebBook][4])

docs.text: Fluorine — People and Intellectual Lineage Henri Moissan Role: In 1886 Moissan successfully isolated elemental Fluorine. MAT interpretation: This demonstrates that isolation of an element may require driving matter away from its more stable naturally occurring compound state. Source: Electronegativity / Bonding Linus Pauling Role: Pauling's electronegativity framework supplies the scale on which Fluorine receives the conventional maximum value: MAT uses this as a bonding descriptor, not as a universal reaction rate predictor. Relevant global source: Robert S. Mulliken Role: Mulliken's molecular orbital framework contributes to the description of: Relevant global source: Fluoropolymers Roy J. Plunkett Role: In 1938 Plunkett unexpectedly discovered polymerized tetrafluoroethylene, leading to PTFE. Important MAT lesson: The material's importance came not from elemental Fluorine alone, but from the polymer architecture of carbon and Fluorine. Source: Noble Gas Fluorides Neil Bartlett Role: In 1962 Bartlett connected the strong oxidizing behavior of PtF6 with xenon's ionization energetics and demonstrated stable xenon containing compounds. Historic conceptual route: Modern qualification: The discovery nevertheless overturned absolute noble gas inertness. Source: Fluorine Nuclear / Imaging Lineage ¹⁸F contributes to: Roles may include future: Do not assign a single "discoverer of 18F PET" where multiple independent developments are involved.
